country.comment: The systematic review evaluates India's national Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) across rural India. Note that 1 of the 20 included articles in Table 1 (Agesa & Agesa, 2019) studies Kenya, and Section 6.6 (PDF pp. 11-12) briefly compares JJM with literature from South Africa, Kenya, Bangladesh, and Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract and Section 1; PDF p. 4, Section 3.3-3.4; Table 1, PDF p. 7

effect_estimate.comment: The review performs purely qualitative thematic synthesis without meta-analysis or pooled/study-level numeric effect estimates.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across 20 synthesized studies on India's Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) improved rural water access, public health, and women's time use, while sustainable and equitable delivery was hindered by infrastructural delays, bureaucratic neglect of pipeline leaks and storage faults, ambiguous responsibilities across local governments, JJM workers, and contractors, institutional overlap, absence of structured grievance redressal mechanisms, and limited Gram Panchayat and community participation where external engineers or contractors dominated decision-making.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 8-11, Sections 6.1-6.4; PDF pp. 12-13, Sections 7-7.1

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <=2 by the systematic review (AMSTAR 2) design ceiling. Rated 1 because this secondary qualitative review collects no primary empirical or field-level process data and reports only high-level thematic/descriptive summaries from secondary literature linking governance, participation, institutional fragmentation, and grievance redressal to rural water delivery outcomes.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 6.3-6.4; PDF p. 13, Section 8; PDF p. 14, Declarations

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines bottom-up/district and region-specific water planning (ELIGIBILITY: planning), infrastructural and bureaucratic maintenance response delays (BURDEN: delay), absence of structured grievance redressal mechanisms and Panchayat-level grievance platforms (ENFORCEMENT: complaint), Gram Panchayat and community participation vs contractor-led decision-making (participation), ambiguity of responsibility and institutional overlap across local government, JJM workers, and contractors (institutional_fragmentation), and cross-sectoral coordination across health, education, and drinking water departments (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, ENFORCEMENT, planning, delay, complaint, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 6.1, 6.3, and 6.4; PDF p. 13, Section 7.1

outcome_flags.comment: Examines Functional Household Tap Connections (formal_connection), rural drinking water access (water_access), sanitation outcomes (sanitation_access), household tap coverage and regional disparities (service_coverage), irregular pressure and reliability (service_reliability), water safety/pathogen monitoring (service_quality), intermittent supply and disruptions (service_continuity), and infrastructural/maintenance response delays (delay).

sample_size.comment: Secondary systematic literature review synthesizing 20 published studies (11 qualitative, 6 quantitative, 3 mixed-methods). No primary household or participant data were collected.
sample_size.value: 20 included articles (from 70 identified records: 62 via database search and 8 via citation searching; 24 unique records screened)

study_design.value: Systematic literature review (PRISMA 2020) with qualitative thematic synthesis
